data.content: PROTOCOL AUDIT — prior implementation plan withdrawn pending protocol redesign. Evidence at shipped main 9237449cf77a: (1) SyncRefConfig reads repo-local knots.remoteRef or KNOTS_REMOTE_REF and otherwise defaults to legacy refs; src/sync_ref.rs:18-30,99-103. No upgrade/version handshake chooses v2. (2) Old push scans every local index/event/snapshot before fetch, then fetches/resets the configured ref, copies every missing file, commits, and pushes HEAD to that same ref; pre-5728 src/replication.rs at 2b028bf1:94-117,149-220,301-360. If an old binary is pointed at knots-v2, it fast-forward resurrects every pruned local file. (3) Sync pushes before pulling; pre-5728 replication.rs:242-253, so a later snapshot/parser failure cannot prevent resurrection. (4) Old pull loads lexicographically latest active/cold snapshots independently only when both watermarks are absent, then scans/diffs A/M paths and advances watermarks; src/sync/apply.rs:102-168 and src/snapshots.rs:141-253. Existing clients ignore deletions; fresh old clients ignore the manifest and the new edge payload. (5) Current 5728 fence runs only in a new binary when the configured ref equals one of two v2 literals; src/replication.rs:233-259 and src/sync_ref.rs:46-50. Its isolation test only proves an explicit push to the legacy ref does not move v2; publication_tests.rs:76-100. It does not model an old binary configured to v2. (6) Repository hooks are local post-merge pull hooks only; src/git_hooks.rs:6-8,72-88. No server receive hook or schema/version gate exists in this repository. Live GitHub has no knots-v2 ref and its sole ruleset targets only the default branch. Therefore local ref switching, CAS activation, and manifest compatibility fields cannot enforce writer upgrades across machines or repositories. Revised prerequisite design: store protocol-two events, index, and snapshots in a generation-scoped namespace old binaries never scan, e.g. .knots/v2/{events,index,snapshots}; new readers/writers ignore legacy .knots/{events,index,snapshots} on the v2 ref and use sparse checkout for the v2 namespace plus manifests. An old binary forced onto v2 may add legacy paths, but cannot mutate or resurrect the semantic v2 namespace; those writes are visibly non-authoritative. The only alternative with the current namespace is a protected active ref writable solely by a validating relay/service, which is not portable to arbitrary Git remotes without new infrastructure. Revised 2af8 sequence after a prerequisite contract change: validate manifest-bound v2 snapshots; transactionally replace projections and replay v2 retained delta plus migrated eligible local events; migrate quarantine baselines; then test with the actual prior binary in default-legacy and forced-v2 modes, fresh clones, pre-cutoff watermarks, corrupt generations, and rollback. Do not implement DB replacement against the current same-path protocol.
